problem.title: Shortest and Lexicographically Smallest Beautiful String

approaches.title: Sliding window over substrings containing exactly k ones
approaches.summary: Maintains a two-pointer window and tracks the number of ones to examine candidate substrings. The initial version additionally tracked a numeric binary value, while later revisions directly compared substring length and lexicographic order and trimmed leading zeros more efficiently.

revisions.commitComment: bin tracking approach supports max of 63 len str
revisions.rawCommitSubject: rust 2904!: bin tracking approach supports max of 63 len str
revisions.shortChangeSummary: Introduced a sliding-window approach that tracks the count of ones and compares candidates using their binary numeric values. This revision was marked wrong and limited binary-value tracking to 63 characters.

revisions.commitComment: hais you can just compare strings...
revisions.rawCommitSubject: rust 2904: hais you can just compare strings...
revisions.shortChangeSummary: Removed binary-value tracking and compared candidate strings directly by length and lexicographic order. Also cleaned up the window implementation and removed debug output.

revisions.commitComment: more idomatic two-pointer & cleaner comparison with tuples
revisions.rawCommitSubject: rust 2904: more idomatic two-pointer & cleaner comparison with tuples
revisions.shortChangeSummary: Refactored the same two-pointer strategy into a forward loop that trims leading zeros before evaluating each candidate. Simplified best-candidate selection with tuple comparison and restored broader test coverage.
